subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why is a change of state described as a physical change rather than a chemical change?
options: The number of particles changes
A new substance is always made
Energy is destroyed during the change
The substance recovers its original properties if the change is reversed
questions.explain: Changes of state are physical: no new substance forms, and the material recovers its original properties if the change is reversed (e.g. water refreezing to ice).

questions.q: Which energy resource is most reliable for continuous large-scale electricity generation?
options: Fossil fuels
Solar
Wave
Wind
questions.explain: Fossil-fuel power stations can run on demand at any time, making them reliable, whereas solar, wind and wave depend on the weather and time of day.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph, what does the gradient of the straight (linear) region represent?
options: The elastic potential energy
The spring constant
The limit of proportionality
The weight of the spring
questions.explain: For the linear region, F = ke, so the gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k. The area under the line gives the elastic potential energy stored.

questions.q: In the specific heat capacity required practical, why is a layer of insulation wrapped around the metal block?
options: To reduce energy lost to the surroundings
To increase the block's mass
To raise the heater's power
To speed up heating
questions.explain: Insulation reduces energy dissipated to the surroundings, so more of the electrical energy supplied raises the block's temperature, giving a more accurate value of c.

questions.q: How did the Sun form?
options: From the explosion of a planet
From a black hole running out of energy
It has always existed unchanged
From a collapsing cloud of dust and gas (a nebula) pulled together by gravity
questions.explain: The Sun formed when a cloud of dust and gas (nebula) was pulled together by gravity. As it collapsed it heated up, eventually starting nuclear fusion.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an energy store?
options: Chemical
Current
Kinetic
Elastic potential
questions.explain: Current is a rate of flow of charge, not an energy store. The stores are kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical, magnetic, electrostatic and nuclear.

questions.q: What is a major environmental drawback of burning fossil fuels for electricity?
options: They release carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
They use up the world's water
They produce radioactive waste
They cannot be transported
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) plus other pollutants, contributing to global warming and acid rain. Radioactive waste is a drawback of nuclear power, not fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Energy and power are the same quantity
Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: For an object (such as the Earth) to stay at a constant temperature, what must be true about its radiation?
options: The rate it absorbs radiation equals the rate it emits radiation
It neither absorbs nor emits radiation
It emits more radiation than it absorbs
It absorbs more radiation than it emits
questions.explain: Temperature stays constant when the power absorbed equals the power emitted. If absorption exceeds emission the object warms; if emission exceeds absorption it cools.

questions.q: During the main sequence stage, what process releases energy in a star's core?
options: Gravitational collapse only
Nuclear fission of uranium
Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
Burning of fuel like a fire (combustion)
questions.explain: Main sequence stars release energy by nuclear fusion, joining hydrogen nuclei to form helium. This is not chemical burning — it is a nuclear process in the core.

questions.q: Why can the efficiency of a real device never be 100%?
options: All devices store chemical energy
Some energy is always dissipated to less useful stores
Power and energy are different quantities
Some energy is always destroyed
questions.explain: Energy is conserved, but some is always dissipated (e.g. as thermal energy through friction or heating), so useful output is always less than total input.

questions.q: What is the activity of a radioactive source?
options: The mass of the source
The rate at which its nuclei decay, measured in becquerel (Bq)
The number of undecayed nuclei remaining
The energy of each emitted particle
questions.explain: Activity is the rate at which nuclei of a source decay, measured in becquerel (Bq), where 1 Bq is one decay per second.

questions.q: What happens to the average kinetic energy of gas particles as the temperature of the gas increases?
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays the same
It depends on the container size
questions.explain: The temperature of a gas is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles: raising the temperature increases their average kinetic energy, so they move faster.

questions.q: What makes a main sequence star (like the Sun) stable for billions of years?
options: It is held together by magnetism
There are no forces acting on it
It is constantly shrinking
The inward force of gravity is balanced by the outward pressure from fusion energy
questions.explain: During the main sequence the inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward force from the expansion of hot gases (energy released by hydrogen fusion). This equilibrium keeps the star stable.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
options: Natural gas
Wind
Coal
Nuclear fuel
questions.explain: Wind is renewable as it is replenished and will not run out. Coal, natural gas and nuclear fuel are finite (non-renewable) resources.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, how do the oscillations relate to the direction the wave travels (energy transfer)?
options: In the same direction as the energy
Perpendicular (at 90°) to the direction of energy transfer
Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
There are no oscillations
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer. In a longitudinal wave they are parallel to it.

questions.q: On a heating graph, the temperature stays constant while a substance boils. What is happening to the energy supplied during this flat section?
options: It is being lost and has no effect
It is reducing the mass of the substance
It is being used to break the bonds between particles (increasing potential energy)
It is being used to increase the particles' kinetic energy
questions.explain: During a change of state the temperature is constant because the energy supplied breaks the bonds/forces between particles (raising potential energy), not their kinetic energy.

questions.q: A stretched elastic band stores energy in which store?
options: Thermal
Magnetic
Elastic potential
Chemical
questions.explain: Stretching or compressing a spring or band stores energy in the elastic potential store.

questions.q: What is nuclear fusion?
options: Two light nuclei joining to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
A large unstable nucleus splitting into two smaller nuclei
A nucleus emitting an alpha particle
An electron joining the nucleus
questions.explain: Fusion is the joining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy (as in the Sun). Fission is the splitting of a large unstable nucleus into smaller ones.

questions.q: Which of the following is a longitudinal wave?
options: A wave on a string
Light
A sound wave in air
A water wave
questions.explain: Sound is a longitudinal wave: the air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer, creating compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: Why does the national grid transmit electricity at very high potential difference and low current?
options: To increase the power generated
To increase the resistance of the cables
To make the current alternate faster
To reduce energy wasted as heat in the cables
questions.explain: Power loss in cables is given by P = I^2 R, so reducing the current greatly reduces energy wasted as heat. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. and lower the current for efficient transmission.

questions.q: In the national grid, what is the role of a step-down transformer near homes?
options: To increase the current in the transmission lines
To convert ac to dc
To raise the voltage for long-distance transmission
To lower the voltage to a safer level for domestic use
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the voltage for efficient transmission; step-down transformers near towns and homes lower the voltage (e.g. to 230 V) so it is safe to use in buildings.
